definitions.meaning: Exactly the same shape and size: every matching side and every matching angle is equal, so one figure fits exactly on the other.
The congruence test where all three pairs of matching sides are equal: sides 6, 8, 10 in one triangle matching 6, 8, 10 in another proves congruence.
The congruence test where two matching angles and the side between them are equal in both triangles.
The same shape at a different size: matching angles are equal and matching lengths share one ratio; areas scale by the square and volumes by the cube of that ratio.
The segment on the opposite side of a chord from the angle between a tangent and that chord; the two angles are equal by the alternate segment theorem.

mechanismSteps: SSS: three sides match: pair each side of one triangle with the equal side of the other (6 with 6, 8 with 8, 10 with 10); three matching pairs leave only one possible shape.
ASA: two angles and the side between: the two equal angles fix the directions of the remaining sides, and the equal included side fixes the size, so the triangles coincide.
Similarity: lengths, areas and volumes: doubling every length keeps the shape, multiplies the area by 2² = 4 and the volume by 2³ = 8.
Angle in a semicircle is a right angle: wherever point C sits on the circle on diameter AB, angle ACB stays 90°.
Centre angle = 2 × circumference angle: on the same chord, a centre angle of 130° pairs with a circumference angle of 65°.
The alternate segment theorem: the angle between the tangent and a chord at the point of contact reappears inside the segment on the far side of the chord.
A common mistake: same area means congruent? A 9 cm by 4 cm rectangle and a 6 cm by 6 cm square share area 36 cm² but their sides do not match, so they are not congruent.
objectives: Prove two triangles congruent using the SSS and ASA tests
Scale lengths, areas and volumes between similar figures using the length ratio
Apply the semicircle, centre-angle and alternate segment circle theorems

trap.explanation: Equal measure feels like equal shape. A long thin rectangle and a square can share the same area while looking completely different, because area counts covering, not outline. Equal area says nothing about shape: congruence needs every matching side and angle. In class, compare the 9 cm by 4 cm rectangle with the 6 cm by 6 cm square: both areas are 36 cm², yet no side of one matches the square's 6 cm sides in a full pairing.
trap.misconception: Two shapes with the same area are congruent.

workedExample: Prove that a triangle with sides 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm is congruent to a triangle with sides 9 cm, 5 cm and 7 cm. Pair the sides in size order: 5 matches 5, 7 matches 7 and 9 matches 9. All three pairs of matching sides are equal, so the triangles are congruent by SSS. Check the trap: the two triangles also have equal area, but that is not the reason - the proof is the three matching sides.
